drafted_from: tools/motion-film-template/tool-rows.json (tool:premix-a-motion-films-soundtrack), do-work/premix_soundtrack.py, test/test_premix_soundtrack.py (RunTest, PlanTest); list:settings read with records:read; the answer was produced by running the script with ffmpeg tones
start_here: Say to your AI: "Mix the soundtrack for my sample film from its cue sheet: the music bed ducked under both voice lines, and three sound effects on their frames." It writes the request file and runs the premix on your computer.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own options list (see pour), or make list:settings from them, and put your film's music file, start, gain windows and loudness choice in its row (record:setting:motion-film-template~film~<film>).
2. Optionally run tool:plan-a-motion-films-soundtrack-premix first to see the ffmpeg commands without making anything.

3. Say "Mix the soundtrack for my film". The AI reads the row with tools:list, writes a request file ({cue_sheet, film_folder, sound_folder, settings, run: true}) and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/motion-film-template/do-work/premix_soundtrack.py < request.json where your recordings are (needs ffmpeg).

4. Read the last line it prints: {"result": {"out", "DUR", "method", "counts", ...}} and play the wav at out. For a two-pass method it also gives measured_i and output_i, the loudness before and after.

worked_examples.title: Two voice lines and three effects mixed to one 6-second wav with no loudness pass
worked_examples.ask: Mix the soundtrack for my sample film from its cue sheet.
worked_examples.given: From test/test_premix_soundtrack.py (its RunTest setup and SHEET) and do-work/premix_soundtrack.py, run on this computer with ffmpeg sine tones standing in for recordings: sound/music/bed.wav (12 s), sound/palette/whoosh.wav, tick.wav, chime.wav, films/sample/assets/vo/l01.wav and l02.wav. The request file holds {"cue_sheet": {"DUR": 6, "VO": [0.5, 2.3], "voiced": [[0.6, 1.8], [2.4, 3.5]], "cues": [[0, "whoosh", -12], [1.25, "tick", -18], [4, "chime", -9]]}, "film_folder": "films/sample", "sound_folder": "sound", "run": true, "settings": {"music": {"file": "{sound}/music/bed.wav", "start": 2, "fade_out": 1.5, "chain": "<the music chain of the film's settings row>"}, "gain": {"base": -6, "duck": -8}, "loudness": {"method": "none"}, "after_mix": "loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11"}}. The AI runs: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/motion-film-template/do-work/premix_soundtrack.py < request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: It prints "wrote films/sample/assets/soundtrack.wav 6.0 s, 3 effects from 3 recordings", and its last line is {"result": {"out": "films/sample/assets/soundtrack.wav", "DUR": 6.0, "method": "none", "gain_segments": [[0.0, -6.0], [0.5, -14], [2.05, -6.0], [2.3, -14], [3.75, -6.0]], "counts": {"voice_lines": 2, "effects": 3, "recordings": 3, "inputs": 6}}}. The file films/sample/assets/soundtrack.wav now exists and lasts 6 seconds.

pour.how: Name the options list you already keep and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than 80% of the kit's fields match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
